theDECORATIVELEDGER_andWhyItIsATWOWAYCON.why: aria-hidden is the strongest instrument-silencing attribute in this product. It removes text from the accessibility tree, from 1.4.3's scope and from the second instrument's computed population in ONE attribute. Left undeclared, using it is indistinguishable from fixing the defect, and the 1.856:1 that made the exemption necessary leaves the record entirely.
soItRefusesInBOTHDIRECTIONS: an aria-hidden text element matching NO entry FAILS the build (kind: undeclared-decorative). A lane cannot quiet a contrast finding by hiding the text.
an entry matching NOTHING across the whole run FAILS the build (kind: exemption-outlived-its-cause), on the same terms a waiver's zero arm does.
and the ratio is recomputed and printed every run even though the element is exempt, so the conformance report states the exemption WITH its measurement.
theDECORATIVELEDGER_andWhyItIsATWOWAYCON.andWhatTheEntryItselfSays: "it does not claim the glyph became easier to see. A sighted reader still reads a divider at 1.856:1, which is the shell's deliberate hairline treatment (var(--sc-line-strong) is a line token, not an ink token). The exemption declares that state rather than repainting it, and the ratio above is printed on every run so the declaration cannot quietly become a claim that the defect is gone."
